:::{.callout-tip}
**Reuben** was the first of the six sons of Jacob and Leah, according to the Book of Genesis. He was a disappointment to Jacob and lost the pre-eminent position which should have been his as Jacob's firstborn. He was the founder of the Israelite Tribe of Reuben. [Wiki](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reuben_(son_of_Jacob))

**Simeon** was the second of the six sons of Jacob and Leah, and the founder of the Israelite tribe of Simeon. Simeon is absent from some of the passages in the Bible which list the other tribes, and some scholars think that it was not initially regarded as a distinct tribe. The Blessing of Moses, before his death, had omitted the Tribe of Simeon because Jacob had castigated him, [Genesis 49:5-7](https://www.bible.com/bible/59/GEN.49.5-7), and because of the affair of Baal-peor. [Wiki](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simeon_(son_of_Jacob))
:::

:::{.callout-tip}
The division between the School of Hillel (Beit Hillel, led by Hillel and later his son Shimon) and the School of Shammai (Beit Shammai) in the Sanhedrin was a foundational 1st-century BCE to 1st-century CE ideological split over Jewish law (Halakha), ethics, and Roman relations.  

- *School of Hillel*: Known for a moderate, flexible, and compassionate approach to Torah interpretation, emphasizing human welfare, humility, and social harmony. 
- *School of Shammai*: Known for a strict, stern, and uncompromising approach, prioritizing rigid textual adherence and intense patriotic/anti-Roman separation.

 The Talmud records over 300 major disputes between the two houses covering ritual purity, marriage, divorce, and holiday observances
:::

## :handshake: Discussion {#sec-discussion}
1. As you watched this episode, which characters or moments stood out to you the most, and why? What was it about those scenes or people that captured your attention?
2. We are introduced to Judas in this episode, although we only discover his identity towards the end. What was your first impression of him? How would you describe his character and motivations? What do you think drives his desire to live a life that matters?
3. The disciples manage to secure the location for the Sermon on the Mount despite numerous obstacles and disagreements. By now, they have seen how God can work through situations that seem impossible from a human perspective. Have you experienced something similar in your own life? 
4. Matthew reflects on how challenging the Sermon on the Mount will be for those who hear it. Jesus explains that he is calling people to a radical change in how they live. Why does Jesus demand so much from those who follow him?
5. In the episode, Jesus makes the Beatitudes personal by connecting each one to the lives and experiences of his disciples. Read [Matthew 5:1–12](https://www.bible.com/bible/59/MAT.5.1-12) again. Which of the Beatitudes resonates with you most? Which do you find the most challenging to live out? Why?
6. When speaking with his mother, Jesus repeats her words from Cana: "If not now, then when?" What makes the Sermon on the Mount such a defining teaching of Christianity, and why has its message continued to resonate across centuries and cultures?

## :thought_balloon: Food for thought {#sec-thought}
1. Judas's business partner often acts as the voice of reason. He is pragmatic about opportunities to get ahead in life and justifies his decisions by appealing to necessity and common sense, while Judas seems more idealistic. Whose perspective do you find yourself agreeing with more?
2. Mary is still dwelling on her recent fall. She says, "I need more words. More tools. I can't let it happen again." What advice does Ramah give her? What would you say to Mary?
3. Jesus thinks about each of his disciples individually. What does Jesus know about you that perhaps no one else does?
4. Jesus is moved when he sees his disciples going out to neighboring towns, distributing handwritten notices and spreading the word about the coming sermon. What does his reaction tell us about how Jesus views [the great comission](https://www.bible.com/bible/59/MAT.28.18-20)?
5. In this episode, Jesus describes the Beatitudes as a map to finding him. If others were to look at your life, which of the Beatitudes would they recognize in you? 
6. Read through the Beatitudes and think of one person in your life who embodies each of the qualities Jesus describes. What can you learn from these people?
